findings.body: The test's comment claims it "asserts the wire between config and gateway, which is the half that would leave the setting inert." But it does not call the `GatewayModel` constructor that reads from `Models` — it manually copies `models.reasoning_effort` into a struct literal and then calls `reasoning_options` on it. This is functionally identical to `off_disables_reasoning_rather_than_asking_for_a_little` above it: both just assert `reasoning_options("off")` returns the disabled JSON. If the constructor were changed to hardcode `reasoning_effort: "high".into()` instead of `reasoning_effort: models.reasoning_effort.clone()`, this test would still pass — exactly the failure it claims to catch. The `SAFETY-adjacent` comment explains the avoidance of env mutation, but the fix is to call the real constructor (wrapping it in a helper that sets the named env var to a dummy value and unsets it afterwards), not to bypass it.
findings.title: Config-to-gateway wiring test bypasses the constructor it claims to cover

value.summary: The change adds a `reasoning_effort` config field, wires it through `reasoning_options` to the OpenRouter gateway, updates default models, and adds pricing rows. The pricing tests are well-anchored and would fail on regression. One new test claims to verify the config-to-gateway wire but manually constructs the struct instead of calling the constructor, so it cannot catch the inert-setting failure it describes.
